html:
Cahulia is the map's spelling of the Cahuilla, an Indigenous people of the inland deserts and mountains of southern California, around the Coachella Valley, Palm Springs and the San Jacinto Mountains. They speak a Uto-Aztecan language.

They lived in a hard land by using it closely: they gathered mesquite beans, acorns and the fruit of the native fan palms around desert oases, and dug walk-in wells to reach water. Spanish missions barely reached them, but American settlement in the later 1800s took most of their land. Several Cahuilla bands hold reservations today; the Agua Caliente band owns much of the land under Palm Springs. Their neighbours include the Luiseño, the Serrano and the Kumeyaay. See Cahuilla.
